transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I keep rechecking and fixing how I look before I go out or get on camera, and it’s starting to make me late and stressed all the time. My sister noticed how much I was struggling with this and convinced me to come in and talk to someone.
When you feel the need to keep checking and fixing your appearance, what is the main worry or thought running through your mind?

Ever since some teammates and relatives teased me about a photo, I can't stop worrying that my jaw looks crooked and my skin looks terrible. I get this overwhelming fear that I look completely ugly or off to other people, which drives me to keep checking the mirror and trying to fix it.
When you ask others about your jaw or skin, do they agree that there is a noticeable problem, or do they tell you they don't see anything wrong?

My friends and family always tell me they don't see anything weird at all and that I look completely normal. It's really frustrating and confusing because, to me, my crooked jaw and bad skin are just so obvious and hard to ignore.

Aside from checking and fixing your appearance, do you experience other repetitive habits or persistent, unwanted thoughts about things like cleanliness, safety, or needing things to be in a specific order?

No, I don't have any worries or habits related to cleanliness, safety, or keeping things in a certain order. All of my stress and checking are strictly focused on my appearance, like trying to fix my face, hair, and clothes before I can go out.

When you feel anxious about being around other people, is it entirely because you worry they will notice your jaw or skin, or do you also worry about things like acting awkwardly or saying the wrong thing?

My anxiety is entirely about my appearance, specifically my crooked jaw and bad skin. I don't really worry about saying the wrong thing or acting awkwardly around others. My main fear is just that people will notice these flaws and judge how I look.
How long have you been experiencing these intense worries about your jaw and skin, and about how many hours a day do you spend thinking about or trying to fix them?

These worries really started when I came to college and began dating, especially after those teasing comments about a photo. I don't keep a strict clock, but I easily lose 20 to 30 minutes every single time I have to get ready for class, soccer, or a video call. Throughout the rest of the day, I find myself constantly zooming in on photos and worrying about my jaw and skin.
Have you ever sought out, or strongly considered, medical treatments, dermatological procedures, or surgeries to fix your jaw or skin?

No, I haven't sought out or really considered any medical treatments, skin procedures, or surgeries for my jaw or skin. I mostly just try to fix or hide how I look on my own in front of the mirror by adjusting my hair and clothes before I go out.

latest_inference.note: The patient's presentation is highly characteristic of Body Dysmorphic Disorder, which is classified under Hypochondriacal Disorder (F45.2) in ICD-10. The patient describes a persistent preoccupation with perceived defects in their physical appearance (crooked jaw and bad skin) that are not noticeable to others. This preoccupation leads to repetitive behaviors (checking mirrors, adjusting clothes/hair, zooming in on photos) and causes significant distress and impairment (lateness, social anxiety secondary to appearance fears). Primary social anxiety disorder and generalized OCD have been ruled out. I have sufficient information to make a confident final diagnosis.
